LESSON: READING 8.2.2 READING THREE LETTER WORDS

Grade: SNE  /  hearing-impairment / PP2
Subject: General
Strand: Strand 8
Topic 8.2: Reading 8.2.2 Reading three letter words
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Reading 8.2.2 Reading three letter words, part of Strand 8 in SNE  /  hearing-impairment / PP2 General.

Key inquiry question: How do we read syllables? 2. Which materials can we use to read syllablles from?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Reading 8.2.2 Reading three letter words together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Self - efficacy as learner sign reads syllables accurately.

● Learning to learn: self discipline as learner works collaboratively to practice reading three letter words.

Values:
● Unity: inclusion as learner with others chant rhymes on syllables in unison.

● Integrity: as learner with others practice fairness in taking turns while blending sounds and reading syllables.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
Ethnic and racial relations as learner works with others in the class harmoniously regardless of their background.

Link to other Activity Areas:

Ability to read is necessary in every learning and so the skill to read cuts across all learning Areas.

Suggested Learning Resources:

Adapted course books, Signed audio visual clips, books, flash cards, charts, pictures, online resources, relevant digital
